stories.standfirst: {winner} takes season {seasonNo} by the narrowest of margins, a lead so slim it could have slipped through a keyhole.
paragraphs: {winnerClub} finished season {seasonNo} in front of {loserClub}, but only just. {winner} took the honours by {margin}, a gap thin enough to vanish with one stray breath, yet wide enough to carry the season home.

For {loser}, this is the cruellest kind of near thing: a campaign played at full stretch and settled by the width of a boot. For {winner}, it is proof that a small advantage, held steadily, still counts as a lead.
Season {seasonNo} of {seasonsTotal} is now in the book. Both managers will spend the break studying the same thin line from opposite sides of it.

pullquote.text: You could not slide newsprint between them, and still one of them found the room.

stories.standfirst: Rarely has so little separated two clubs, and rarely has it meant so much to the one on the right side.
paragraphs: {winnerClub} closed the season on {winnerPoints} against the {loserPoints} of {loserClub}, and the gap between those two figures is the whole story. {winner} wins season {seasonNo}, and the margin is as narrow as football allows.
It would be easy to call it luck, and it would be wrong. A lead this small is earned in the quiet weeks, and {loser} will know that the same quiet weeks were available to both sides.
The rivalry now carries a fresh grievance and a fresh bragging right in equal measure. Neither will fade before the next season begins, and neither manager will want it to.

pullquote.text: A hair is not much to win by, but it is more than nothing.

stories.standfirst: {loser} pushed all the way to the line, and {winner} still had just enough left to hold the lead in season {seasonNo}.
paragraphs: Applause is due to {loserClub} before the winner is named. {loser} drove the season to its very last breath, and only the thinnest of margins, {margin} in all, kept {winnerClub} and {winner} in front.
That is the measure of this rivalry. Neither side can relax, because the distance between a good season and a great one has shrunk to almost nothing, and both managers have now seen it up close.
{loser} leaves season {seasonNo} with nothing to be ashamed of and every reason to be dangerous. The next chapter will begin with a point to prove, and a short walk to prove it.

pullquote.text: Second by a whisker is still a loud kind of second.

stories.standfirst: Season {seasonNo} was a tightrope walk across {seasonsTotal} seasons of ambition, and {winner} reached the far side with an inch to spare.
paragraphs: There are seasons that sprawl and seasons that squeeze, and this was a squeeze. {winnerClub} crossed the line ahead of {loserClub} by the narrowest of margins, and {winner} will accept that inch with both hands.
The drama lies in how little room there was for error. One tentative step and the order reverses, which is why {winner} wins this one on nerve as much as on skill.
{loser} will look at the width of the gap and see an invitation. The tightrope is still strung, the next season is waiting, and the net remains a long way down.

pullquote.text: On a rope that thin, the only thing to do is keep walking.

stories.standfirst: A photo finish with no photograph: {winner} edges {loser} in season {seasonNo} and nobody can say it was easy.
paragraphs: Had there been a camera on the line, the picture would have needed a magnifying glass. {winnerClub} edged {loserClub} by {margin}, and the verdict of season {seasonNo} belongs to {winner} by the smallest possible stretch.
Those who prefer decisive outcomes will be disappointed. Those who love a rivalry will be delighted, because this is how grudges are grown: in small, stubborn portions that nobody can quite dismiss.
{loser} will say, with some justice, that it was close enough to touch. {winner} will reply, equally fairly, that touching is not the same as winning.

pullquote.text: Close enough to touch, and that is exactly where it stayed.
pullquote.who: The tea lady at the training ground

stories.standfirst: Some seasons are won by a lunge and some by a leaning shoulder; this one, for {winner}, was a leaning shoulder.
paragraphs: {winner} did not run away with season {seasonNo}, and nobody in the press box pretended otherwise. {winnerClub} leaned on {loserClub} for the whole contest and came out ahead by the narrowest of margins.
A lean is a patient thing. It asks for pressure without panic, and it rewards the manager who trusts it when the other side pushes back, which {loser} certainly did with great spirit.
The rivalry has gained a new lesson, which is that small leads are still leads. Season {seasonNo} of {seasonsTotal} will be remembered less for its size than for its stubbornness.

pullquote.text: Nobody wins by a lean unless they believe in the lean.

stories.standfirst: A chess game decided by a single pawn: {winnerClub} take season {seasonNo} from {loserClub} in the tightest finish imaginable.
paragraphs: Chess players know the feeling: every piece is traded, every plan is parried, and the game turns on one small advantage. That is how {winner} won season {seasonNo}, ahead of {loser} by the narrowest of margins.
The pawn was worth {margin}, and it was enough. {winnerClub} will now enter the next season with a quiet edge, while {loserClub} will be studying the position and looking for the move that got away.
Nothing is decided, and that is the pleasure of it. The board is reset, the clocks are running, and a pawn is still only a pawn until somebody promotes it.

pullquote.text: Every great game is won by something that looked too small to matter.

stories.standfirst: The tide went out on season {seasonNo} and {winner} was still standing, though the water had not gone far.
paragraphs: For most of the season the sea level between {winnerClub} and {loserClub} barely changed. When it finally settled, {winner} stood a fraction higher, and that fraction, {margin} by the Gazette's reckoning, was the season.
A margin like this is not a weakness in the winner. It is the sign of an opponent who refused to drop away, and {loser} deserves the credit for keeping the water so high.
Tides come back, as every harbour knows. Season {seasonNo} is {winner}'s, but the next one is already rolling in with {loserClub} firmly in its sights.

pullquote.text: The sea does not care who stood highest, only who stayed.

stories.standfirst: A ledger balanced to the last digit: {winner} closes season {seasonNo} ahead of {loser} by the thinnest sum a book can show.
paragraphs: The auditors have finished, and the Gazette can report that {winnerClub} leads {loserClub} for season {seasonNo} by {margin}. It is the smallest balance a book can show without being empty, and {winner} signs it with relief.
Accountants love a tidy result, but rivals love an untidy one. {loser} will go over every line of the season and find a dozen places where the sum could have come out differently.
Such a thin ledger cannot be spent freely. {winner} holds the credit for now, and it will take careful housekeeping through the rest of the {seasonsTotal} seasons to keep it.

pullquote.text: Credit is credit, even when you can barely see it in the book.
pullquote.who: The tea lady at the training ground

stories.standfirst: Nobody can accuse {winner} of luck in season {seasonNo}, nor accuse {loser} of anything but a rival worth having.
paragraphs: It is the kind of result that invites argument, and the Gazette is happy to join in. {winnerClub} won season {seasonNo} by the narrowest of margins, and {loserClub} was on its heels for every step of the way.
What is certain is that both managers produced seasons good enough to win. One of them simply ended a hair higher, and that hair now decides who gets to tell the story at the next meeting.
{loser} may take comfort in how rarely a rival gets this close without being passed. The coming season promises a rematch that neither side needs to be asked twice about.

pullquote.text: A rival you can barely separate is the best gift in the game.

stories.standfirst: Turn the page on season {seasonNo} and the margin is still the first thing you notice: {winner} by the narrowest of margins.
paragraphs: Every rivalry has chapters that stay in the memory, and this is likely to be one of them. {winner} won season {seasonNo} for {winnerClub} by {margin}, a slender lead that sits in the record like a pressed flower.
In the long story of {winner} and {loser}, the close seasons are the ones that get retold. Nobody remembers a rout for long, but everybody remembers the year it nearly went the other way.
The archive has room for many more of these. With {seasonsTotal} seasons to be played, the narrow ones may yet prove the most important pages of all.

pullquote.text: The thin chapters are always the ones people reread.

stories.standfirst: The pendulum swung toward {winnerClub} in season {seasonNo}, but only a short way, and it is still trembling.
paragraphs: Rivalries behave like pendulums, and this one has just swung in favour of {winner}. The arc was short, a matter of {margin} over {loserClub}, but a short swing is still a swing, and the clock has moved.
{loser} will feel the pull of it, and so will {winner}. A pendulum that has barely moved is also one that can return in a heartbeat, so nobody should mistake a narrow lead for a safe one.
The next season begins from a place of delicate balance. Whoever pushes first and hardest will find the pendulum answering, and the Gazette will be watching for the first tremor.

pullquote.text: It only moved a little, but everybody in the room felt it.

stories.standfirst: It took until the final line of the chapter, but {winner} has won season {seasonNo} and {loser} will want a sequel.
paragraphs: A good novel keeps its secret until the last page, and season {seasonNo} did precisely that. {winnerClub} turned the final paragraph in front of {loserClub}, the lead measured in the smallest unit the game offers.
{winner} will read the ending with pleasure. {loser} will read it twice, looking for the sentence that could have been written differently, and finding, as every reader does, that it was close.
The story now continues into the next season, with {seasonsTotal} in all to tell it. The Gazette suspects the author has not yet decided how it ends, and neither have the managers.

pullquote.text: The best endings are the ones that leave you reaching for the next chapter.

stories.standfirst: Credit where it is due: {winner} won season {seasonNo} fairly, narrowly and without a hint of fortune.
paragraphs: No one should say {winner} was fortunate. {winnerClub} finished season {seasonNo} ahead of {loserClub} by {margin}, and the small size of the lead takes nothing from the quality of the work behind it.
Equally, no one should say {loser} fell short. A season this tight is a tribute to both sides, and it speaks well of the Showdown that two friends can push each other to the very edge.
Respect flows both ways, and so does ambition. The next season will arrive with handshakes still warm and appetites sharper than before, which is exactly how the best rivalries should run.

pullquote.text: Win by a mile or an inch, the trophy does not ask which.
pullquote.who: The tea lady at the training ground

stories.standfirst: A narrow win feeds the appetite rather than quenching it, and season {seasonNo} has left both managers hungry.
paragraphs: {winner} has taken season {seasonNo} for {winnerClub}, ahead of {loserClub} by the narrowest of margins, and the usual warm afterglow of victory is already giving way to something more restless.
That is the effect of a lead this small. It cannot be admired for long, because it demands to be defended, and {loser} knows it can be taken back with a single decent run.
Expect an appetising next season. {winner} will play to protect the edge, {loser} will play to remove it, and the Gazette has cleared a generous space on the front page for whatever follows.

pullquote.text: A narrow win is a promise to do it all again, only harder.
